base_sha_policy: freeze main SHA at execution start; all candidates must derive from that SHA

candidates.hypothesis: Implement SELECT OPTIONAL semantics for missing sequential files: status 05 and correct creation/EOF behavior; non-optional OPEN EXTEND must not silently create a missing file.
candidates.evidence: docs/EXTERNAL_BENCHMARK_FAILURE_ANALYSIS.md: at least 234 cases exposed to file-I/O omissions; GnuCOBOL documentation states non-OPTIONAL INPUT/I-O/EXTEND missing file yields status 35, OPTIONAL yields status 05 and OPTIONAL EXTEND/I-O creates the file.
candidates.qualification: Merged into main before paired 1,000-case validation; its 251/500 holdout-only result is not a combined record and is now part of the main baseline.

candidates.hypothesis: A second OPEN on an already-open file must return status 41 and preserve the original handle and open mode instead of replacing the live handle.
candidates.evidence: GnuCOBOL Programmer's Guide: attempting to OPEN a file that is already open returns file status 41; current _cobol_open overwrites the open handle map without checking this state.

candidates.hypothesis: Parse one COBOL OPEN statement containing multiple mode groups (for example INPUT file-A and OUTPUT file-B) without applying the first mode to every file.
candidates.evidence: Current translate_statement handles only the first mode group and extracts all identifiers from the remaining text as filenames. This can interpret OUTPUT as a file name and open an output file in INPUT mode. COBOL OPEN syntax permits multiple mode groups in one statement.

ci.failure_cause: mode-token regex split identifiers such as INPUT-FILE at the hyphen; this made generated _cobol_open receive FILE instead of INPUT-FILE and caused four runtime tests to fail.
ci.revision: mode keyword matching now excludes adjacent word and hyphen characters

candidates.hypothesis: Correct STRING DELIMITED BY ZEROES so it recognizes the ZEROES spelling and terminates on the COBOL character '0', not NUL.
candidates.evidence: An existing isolated branch contains a minimal regression for WS-SOURCE='A0B     '; the main translator currently maps ZERO/ZEROS to NUL and does not accept ZEROES in the delimiter token regex.

benchmark.qualification: no raw-score improvement; zero regressions still unproven

candidates.hypothesis: Translate arithmetic expressions in COBOL reference-modification start offsets rather than treating the entire expression as a single data-name.
candidates.evidence: Existing isolated candidate-v3 fixture showed WS-TEXT(WS-START + WS-OFFSET * 2:2) must evaluate to 'CD'; current main normalizes the entire offset as one name.

benchmark.qualification: not_yet_qualified: +1 raw match only; zero-regression case comparison is still required

candidates.hypothesis: Translate arithmetic expressions in COBOL reference-modification lengths rather than treating the entire length as a single data-name.
candidates.evidence: Existing isolated candidate-v3 fixture showed WS-TEXT(1:WS-LENGTH + WS-EXTRA * 2) must produce 'ABC'; current main normalizes the full length as one name.

benchmark.qualification: no raw-score improvement; zero regressions still unproven

candidates.hypothesis: Parse COBOL data declarations whose level number (such as 01) is placed on its own physical line and whose data-name/PIC clause follows on the next line.
candidates.evidence: An existing isolated parser branch contains the pending-level implementation; current main only accepts complete declarations matching RE_VAR on a single line.

benchmark.qualification: no raw-score improvement; zero regressions unproven

candidates.hypothesis: Implement sequential REWRITE at the most recently read record position, requiring OPEN I-O and a prior successful READ, with statuses 49, 43, 44 and 00.
candidates.evidence: GnuCOBOL Programmer's Guide section 7.8.37: REWRITE requires OPEN I-O, a prior READ for sequential organization, and cannot be used with LINE SEQUENTIAL. GnuCOBOL status codes 43/44/49 are documented.

ci.failure_cause: three assertions compared actual newline characters against literal backslash-n strings
ci.revision: fixed test expected strings; runtime implementation unchanged

candidates.hypothesis: Track per-file EOF state so the first unsuccessful sequential READ returns status 10 and another READ before reopen returns status 46.
candidates.evidence: GnuCOBOL sequential file status references document status 10 at end and status 46 for sequential READ with no valid next record after AT END has already been reached.

ci.failure_cause: the regression expected literal backslash-n sequences rather than actual newline characters
ci.revision: corrected expected output string; runtime logic unchanged

candidates.hypothesis: Support WRITE record FROM literal by moving the literal into the record area before writing, while preserving existing identifier-based FROM behavior.
candidates.evidence: The current WRITE parser accepts only a data-name after FROM, although COBOL syntax allows a literal or identifier. The runtime already serializes the record area, so the literal must first be moved into that record.

ci.failure_cause: the new regression expected literal backslash-n rather than the line-sequential newline
ci.revision: corrected expected file contents to include an actual newline

candidates.hypothesis: Implement ACCEPT FROM DATE, DATE YYYYMMDD, DAY, DAY-OF-WEEK and TIME using the host clock and COBOL-compatible output formats.
candidates.evidence: The current Python translator only recognizes ACCEPT target from stdin; the date/time source forms fall through as unsupported statements.

candidates.hypothesis: Implement INSPECT identifier REPLACING ALL/FIRST literal BY literal, preserving occurrence count semantics.
candidates.evidence: The current translator supports INSPECT CONVERTING and TALLYING but has no REPLACING handler; COBOL supports ALL and FIRST replacement modes.

candidates.hypothesis: UNSTRING TALLYING IN must add the number of populated receiving fields to the existing tally value instead of replacing it.
candidates.evidence: Current translate_statement assigns min(len(parts), targets) directly to the tally item. COBOL TALLYING IN is an accumulating counter; a nonzero initial value is lost.

candidates.hypothesis: Honor UNSTRING WITH POINTER for the single-delimiter, non-ALL subset by starting at the 1-based pointer and advancing it past consumed fields and delimiters.
candidates.evidence: The current translator extracts POINTER but never uses it; it always splits from the beginning of the source and leaves the pointer unchanged.
candidates.scope_limit: Multiple delimiters and ALL-pointer combinations are not implemented by this candidate.

candidates.hypothesis: For a single-delimiter, single-receiver UNSTRING, populate DELIMITER IN with the delimiter consumed and COUNT IN with the number of characters moved.
candidates.evidence: Main parses neither DELIMITER IN nor COUNT IN; an existing experimental branch exposed these clauses but did not assign their values. This revision adds both assignments for the explicitly scoped single-receiver subset.
candidates.scope_limit: One receiving field, one delimiter, no ALL; per-receiver options and multiple delimiters are not covered.

candidates.hypothesis: Read ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL files as fixed-width records using the FD record width, while retaining line-based reads for LINE SEQUENTIAL files.
candidates.evidence: The current _cobol_read always calls handle.readline(), which incorrectly treats a sequential fixed-width file without line separators as one record. The regression uses two adjacent four-byte records with no newline.
